definitions.definition: (colloquial, US) A veteran (a former soldier or other member of armed forces).

quote.citation: 1952, Ralph Ellison, Invisible Man, Penguin Books (2014), page 73:
quote.text: “A former soldier, sir. A vet. Theyʼre all vets, a little shellshocked.”

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Possibly by analogy from Etymology 1, in the sense of "verifying the soundness [of an animal]"

definitions.definition: To thoroughly check or investigate particularly with regard to providing formal approval.

quote.citation: 1980 March 10, Antony Jay, Jonathan Lynn, “The Economy Drive”, in Yes, Minister, season 1, episode 3, spoken by Jim Hacker and Humphrey Appleby (Paul Eddington and Nigel Hawthorne):
quote.text: Sir Humphrey Appleby: Nevertheless we do not admit it (the existence of MI6). Not everyone round this table has been vetted (pun). / Jim Hacker: I thought that's something you do to cats (laugh track). / Sir Humphrey Appleby: Yes indeed, but not ferrets, Minister (laugh track).
